claims: The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team won the school's first and only NCAA championship.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team defeated Seton Hall 80–79 in overtime on April 3, 1989.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team was led by interim coach Steve Fisher after Bill Frieder's departure.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team was led by Consensus All-American Glen Rice.
Glen Rice set an NCAA tournament record with 184 points.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team had a 30–7 overall record.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team had a 12–6 record in the Big Ten.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team was ranked 10th in the final AP Poll.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team entered the NCAA Tournament as a #3 seed in the Southeast Region.
Rumeal Robinson hit two free throws with three seconds left in overtime to defeat Seton Hall 80–79.
Steve Fisher took over just before the NCAA Tournament.
Steve Fisher finished with a 6–0 record.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team defeated Xavier 92–87 in the first round of the NCAA Tournament.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team defeated South Alabama 91–82 in the second round of the NCAA Tournament.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team defeated North Carolina 92–87 in the Sweet 16 of the NCAA Tournament.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team defeated Virginia 102–65 in the Elite Eight of the NCAA Tournament.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team defeated Illinois 83–81 in the Final Four of the NCAA Tournament.
Glen Rice was named NCAA Tournament Most Outstanding Player.
Glen Rice set the all-time Big Ten scoring record.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team led the nation in field goal percentage with 56.6%.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team set a Big Ten conference record for single-season points with 3393.
The 1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team set a Big Ten conference record for single-season assists with 745.
